subject: Oceanography
title: Rip Currents
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Rip Currents.

hook.text: Rip currents kill more beachgoers than sharks, hurricanes, and tornadoes combined—over 100 per year in the US.

buildup.text: When waves push water toward shore, it piles up—and must flow back out somewhere.

discovery.text: Rip currents are narrow channels of fast-flowing water heading seaward through the surf zone.

twist.text: They can reach speeds of 2.5 m/s—faster than an Olympic swimmer—dragging people offshore quickly.

climax.text: To escape, swim parallel to shore—rips are narrow, and just a few meters sideways frees you.

punchline.text: Don't fight the current—swim sideways to safety.

quiz.question: How should you escape a rip current?
